plain_english_policy: Enactment of this bill would amend the Alabama Constitution to strictly prohibit abortion in all circumstances except two specific exceptions: when an extreme medical emergency threatens the life of the pregnant woman, or when the pregnancy results from rape or incest. The policy direction is a significant tightening of reproductive rights restrictions by elevating these prohibitions to constitutional status rather than statutory law.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The enactment would legally bar abortion for any reason other than saving the mother's life in an extreme emergency, cases of rape, or cases of incest. It establishes that causing or participating in such prohibited abortions is a Class B felony.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsor advanced the bill to propose this constitutional amendment.
evidence_quotes: "Except in an extreme case of medical emergency where the life of the mother is threatened by the pregnancy or where there is rape or incest, any person... who causes or participates in the abortion of an unborn child shall be guilty of a Class B felony."

"To propose an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, to prohibit abortion except in an extreme case where the pregnancy threatens the life of the mother or where there is rape or incest; and to provide a penalty for a violation of this amendment."
